title: Stalk continuity for fixed pulled-back module sheaves
statement: For a commutative ring Λ, k:W→S, G∈Sh(W_et,Λ), a small cofiltered D:I→Over W with affine transitions and qcqs structure maps to S, and a scheme-limit cone c with qcqs structure map to S, let g_i and g be the structure maps and G_i,G_c the pullbacks of G [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. Fix q∈ℤ and a geometric stalk given by S.uliftPointSmallEtale(s). Every element of (R^qg_*G_c)_s is the image under the canonical transition [def-sbc-module-higher-image-transitions] of some element of (R^qg_i,*G_i)_s. If an element at i maps to zero at the limit, there exist j and f:j→i such that its transition along D(f) is zero at j. This is the unchanged source theorem higherDirectImage_limit, the pulled-back module-sheaf case of Tag 09Z1.

proof.text: Use canonical transition coherence to define the functor K:I^op→Sh(S_et,Λ) with the specified higher-image objects, and define its cocone B with the limit higher image as vertex and the canonical projection transitions as legs. The identity and composition equations prove the functor laws; cone naturality and composition coherence prove cocone naturality.

For each affine etale V, apply affine continuity with identity presentation isomorphisms to K and B. Apply affine-basis colimit detection to assemble an IsColimit B from all these evaluated universal properties.

The geometric sheafFiber is a left adjoint to the skyscraper functor, so it preserves the colimit. The module forgetful functor preserves filtered colimits of this small shape by the universe-shrink lemma. Mathlib Concrete.isColimit_exists_rep gives an element at a stage representing each element at the limit. To detect zero, compare the given stage element with zero at the same stage and apply Concrete.isColimit_exists_of_rep_eq. The resulting common stage and its arrow give the required j→i; module maps take zero to zero.
